title: Explicit minimal generators for the rational-function-evaluation vanishing ideal
author: Ivan Hu, Dieter van Melkebeek, and Andrew Morgan
work: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
source_version: Theory of Computing20 (2024), Article1, publisher source publicationJuly 18, 2024; DOI10.4086/toc.2024.v020a001

source_locator.proof_scope: Complete authored Sections3–4 generating-set argument, Zoom Lemma, cored hitting proof and rational-function helper; all full article definitions/context retained.

difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a determinantal generating family and reduces arbitrary polynomials to a fixed-core normal form without assuming the target ideal characterization. The nonroutine remaining obligation is to prove that every nonzero cored remainder is hit, using the authors’ full Zoom Lemma and its extremal degree-pattern construction in Sections3–4; this goes beyond ordinary qualification-level ideal computations.

source_check.note: Full original Sections1–9 and bibliography are retained. Selected Theorem1.3 includes both the complete generating family and minimum-size fixed-core family. Section3 supplies determinant construction, cored reduction and final proof; Section4 supplies the full Zoom Lemma and the proof of the cored hitting claim. All source-local core is editable and retained. No independent mathematical refereeing or proof repair.
